issues.description: Return-type mismatch for getAllPersons breaks the intended contract and ordering semantics. The problem statement and client/server REST endpoints expect/get/send a List<Person> for GET /persons (a JSON array), and the template PersonService declares getAllPersons(...) to return List<Person>. However, the solution implementation of PersonService changes the method signature to return Set<Person>. Meanwhile the solution PersonResource.getAllPersons(...) still declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and forwards the service result directly. This inconsistency (List vs. Set) will: (1) cause a compile-time generic type mismatch between PersonResource and PersonService, (2) change semantics by using a Set (which does not preserve ordering) thereby nullifying the sorting behavior students are asked to implement, and (3) confuse students about whether getAllPersons should return a List or a Set.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep getAllPersons returning a List<Person> so it matches the problem statement, template, and client expectations, and so sorting is meaningful. Concretely: change the solution PersonService.getAllPersons signature back to public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) and return the sortedList (or Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList)) instead of a Set. Alternatively, if using a Set is intended, update PersonResource and the client to accept and document a Set and adapt the REST JSON contract accordingly — but the simpler and semantically correct fix is to return a List to preserve order and match the exercised API contract.
